newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Telkom SA term loan BB plus long term.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Telkom SA term loan BB plus long term.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Monday it assigned its BB plus long-term rating to the US$175 million term loan (due September 2001), signed on Monday between Telkom SA Ltd (Telkom) and a syndicate of banks led by Credit Suisse and Sumitomo Bank Ltd.
"The outlook on this rating is positive," S&P said in a statement.

"The rating and outlook assigned are equalised with the group's existing corporate credit rating and outlook statement, as this unsecured bank loan ranks equally with Telkom's other unsecured debt and offers no material credit enhancement features," S&P said.

This foreign currency rating of Telkom's bank term loan reflects the group's virtual monopoly position within South African telecommunications, its current government ownership, and a supportive regulatory environment, S&P said.
The rating remains constrained by the Republic of South Africa's long-term foreign currency rating for the time being, S&P said.

"Positive rating factors are offset to a degree by Telkom's high debt levels, and significant capital expenditure requirements needed to rapidly expand telephone availability within rural and under privileged sectors of the community," S&P said.
The government of the Republic has specific objectives in this regard as part of its reconstruction and development program, S&P said.

Moreover, the government's ownership of Telkom is due to fall from 100 percent via a part-privatisation program as part of a national telecommunication policy that will lead to the sector being opened to regulated competition over time, S&P said.
An upgrade of the Republic of South Africa's long-term foreign currency rating would probably lead to an upgrade of Telkom's rating, S&P said.

Despite plans for market liberalisation, Telkom is expected to continue to maintain a significant share of a growing market, to improve service quality and efficiency, and to benefit from growing telephony penetration and usage, S&P said.
